subsystems.name: Neural recording
subsystems.role: capture the activity patterns that accompany a subjective experience in the source brain.
parts: non-invasive imaging such as fMRI (slow) or implanted arrays (fast but invasive)

subsystems.name: Decoding model
subsystems.role: convert raw activity into a representation of what the person is experiencing.

subsystems.name: Encoding and stimulation
subsystems.role: write the corresponding pattern into the target brain.
parts: implanted microelectrodes for electrical or optical stimulation

subsystems.name: Cross-brain alignment
subsystems.role: a person's neural code for 'red' or 'warm' is not identical to anyone else's, so the two must be matched.

subsystems.name: Communication link
subsystems.role: carry the decoded pattern between the two participants in real time.

subsystems.name: Verification and safety layer
subsystems.role: checks whether the received experience actually matches, and limits harm.

buildSteps.title: Choose one simple sensation
buildSteps.detail: Start with something measurable — a faint touch, a flash of light — rather than a complex feeling such as grief.

buildSteps.title: Record the source pattern
buildSteps.detail: Show the stimulus repeatedly to the source person and record which neurons fire, in what order and at what rate.

buildSteps.title: Build a decoder
buildSteps.detail: Train software to recognise that pattern in real time from the recorded signal alone.

buildSteps.title: Build a writer
buildSteps.detail: Find the stimulation parameters in the target brain that evoke a comparable report, then tune them by trial.

buildSteps.title: Align the two brains
buildSteps.detail: Because no two brains wire up identically, run both people through the same calibration set and build a mapping between their representations.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: Link decoder to stimulator so the pattern flows in real time, and check whether the target reports the same thing.

buildSteps.title: Test without feedback
buildSteps.detail: Hide from the target what the source saw, so a correct answer cannot come from ordinary sight or hearing.

buildSteps.title: Scale richness
buildSteps.detail: Only if single sensations transfer reliably would the approach be extended toward whole experiences.

prerequisites.why: non-invasive methods are too coarse and implanted arrays degrade over months to years.

prerequisites.tech: A theory linking neural activity to subjective experience
prerequisites.why: the 'hard problem' of why firing patterns feel like anything at all is unsolved; without it, transfer cannot be verified in principle.
electrical and magnetic stimulation can trigger crude sensations but not yet recreate a specific pattern.
vision and speech have been partly decoded in research settings, but each system needs heavy per-person training.
the decoding and stimulation loop must run in milliseconds, which current hardware can do.

pathway.milestone: simple motor or decision signals sent between two people using EEG and magnetic stimulation
pathway.unlocks: proof that a brain-to-brain channel can work at all.

pathway.milestone: restoring or sharing basic sensory percepts in paralysed or blind patients
pathway.unlocks: detailed maps of how stimulation parameters correspond to reported experience.

pathway.milestone: bidirectional transfer of a controlled, calibrated sensation between healthy volunteers
pathway.unlocks: evidence on whether two brains can be aligned closely enough to share an experience.

pathway.milestone: transfer of richer, more subjective experiences
pathway.unlocks: direct empathy and shared knowledge — or, if the neural code proves not to be shareable, the demonstration that qualia transfer is impossible in practice.
